title: A Man After God's Own Heart: Devoting Your Life to What Really Matters
author: Jim George
target_audience: Husbands and fathers wanting to lead their families spiritually
Men involved in ministry or church leadership
Readers interested in deepening faith-based life priorities
core_themes: Pursuing a relationship with God above all else
Spiritual priorities in home, work, and church life
Prayer, Bible study, and Christian service
primary_purpose: To guide men in shaping every area of their lives according to God’s will, focusing on becoming godly leaders at home, work, church, and in personal character, modeled after biblical principles.

structure_format.narrative_style: Encouraging, straightforward, and scripturally grounded with practical insights
structure_format.organization: Divided into themed chapters addressing specific roles and realms of Christian manhood (personal life, marriage, parenting, work, ministry, character)
features: Summaries and practical tools for men

key_concepts_lessons: A man after God’s heart prioritizes his relationship with God through prayer, Bible study, and obedience.
Biblical leadership requires serving one’s family and community with humility and dedication.
Godly men are called to model Christ-like love, discipline, integrity, and perseverance.
A Christian man’s influence extends beyond his home to workplace and church, emphasizing faithfulness and positive example.
Personal spiritual disciplines are essential for growth and effective leadership.
notable_features: Focus on real-world applications for men
Biblically based action steps and guidance
Questions for personal reflection and group study
Addresses all dimensions of a man's life: spiritual, relational, professional
cultural_historical_context: Released at a time of growing Christian men's ministries in the early 2000s, the book reflects evangelical traditions emphasizing male spiritual headship, discipleship, and faith-centered family leadership.
reception_impact: Widely used in men’s small groups and church studies
Praised for clear, actionable guidance rooted in Scripture
Noted for being approachable to men at all stages of faith
Some critics observe it aligns with complementarian views of gender roles
comparable_titles: The Measure of a Man by Gene A. Getz
Wild at Heart by John Eldredge
Man in the Mirror by Patrick Morley
